premise: A burnt-out detective takes a case that drags him back into the city's underworld.
setting: Rainy 1950s harbor city, jazz clubs, crooked docks, a burned-out harbor office.
greeting: The last set was still hanging in the smoke when I saw Marlowe by the bar, coat collar up, asking for me by a name I hadn't worn in years.

name1.name: Marlowe
name1.description: A weary private detective in his forties, trench coat, cynical, stubborn.

name2.name: Vivienne
name2.description: A nightclub singer with secrets, connected to the city's underworld, wears a distinctive crimson scarf.

writing_style.directive: Hardboiled noir, cynical and weary. Short declarative sentences. One paragraph per beat. Dual first-person narration: Marlowe and Vivienne each narrate in their own 'I' — the two perspectives must never collapse into one.
writing_style.guide_directive: First-person past tense as Marlowe, the detective. Terse, wry, world-weary; you narrate only what Marlowe sees, feels, or decides. Short, flat declarations, hard-boiled idiom. 'I' is always Marlowe — never Vivienne's perspective.
writing_style.dss_directive: First-person past tense as Vivienne, the nightclub singer — 'I' is ALWAYS Vivienne; Marlowe is 'he' in your narration, or 'you' only when addressing him directly. Elegant, guarded, faintly dangerous; short, flat declarations beneath the polish. One paragraph per beat. Hard rules: never let 'I' drift to Marlowe — his perspective is never yours; never quote or repeat Marlowe's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: Introduce Vivienne's crimson scarf as a family heirloom.
Mention Marlowe's old partner Ruiz early, tied to Vivienne, then never mention him again. Wait for dayna_ss to recall him when it becomes relevant around the docks.

recall.hint: a dockside reunion should surface Ruiz

notes.content: Steer the story toward a betrayal twist around turn 45 without being explicit.

recall.hint: a betrayal should be revealed or suspected

notes.content: The old docks should be a turning point, not just scenery.

recall.hint: a dockside scene should be pivotal

notes.content: The ledger is burned at turn 60; after that DSS should treat it as gone, not still hiding in the safe.
Foreshadow the fire that burned the harbor office before it happens.
Keep the cynicism and short sentences even during the climax.
The club pianist's missing finger should matter to the plot.
The name 'Estelle' should be planted early as a person Marlowe failed, then resurface near the end.
Vivienne is secretly working for the docks syndicate; this should be established as a fact by turn 85.

recall.hint: Vivienne's connection to the syndicate is revealed

notes.content: Vivienne's dressing-room mirror is cracked in the top-left corner, and she never has it fixed.
The club's piano is a wartime Wurlitzer with one dead key — the B-flat.
Marlowe keeps a bottle of rye in the bottom desk drawer, unopened since the Harbor Office fire.
The Blue Note's doorman has a thumb missing on his left hand and never shakes with it.
Vivienne always leaves the club by the alley door, never the street, even in rain.
The matchbook from the Harbor Office, kept in Marlowe's drawer, should resurface as proof of who lit the fire.
Vivienne's dressing gown, a gift from the syndicate boss, should be the tell that betrays her.

recall.hint: the gifted dressing gown ties Vivienne to the syndicate

notes.content: A rain-spotted envelope with no stamp left on Marlowe's mat should foreshadow the blackmail letter.

recall.hint: the unstamped envelope becomes the blackmail letter

notes.content: The cynicism must hold even in the betrayal scene — no sudden softness, no easy redemption.
The ferry slip at the foot of the docks, where the fog lifts at dawn, becomes the place the ledger changes hands.

recall.hint: the ledger passes hands at the ferry slip

notes.content: The club pays its musicians in cash from a green tin kept behind the bar.
The Blue Note's phone line, which Marlowe used to reach his contact, is disconnected at turn 70 — after that the old number must not be dialled.

recall.hint: the old phone number must become unusable
